tickets.title: Demonstrate durable multi-process foundations
acceptance: Independent processes produce one event and one projection intent for duplicate submission.
Warm cached bodies cannot bypass current removal state or a database outage.
Worker claims and quota reservations survive contention with conservation and stale-owner rejection.

tickets.title: Boot an authenticated PostgreSQL node
acceptance: A second process can use the same intended instance database; a mismatched service key fails startup.
Identity proof binds nonce and configured endpoint; secrets are not returned or logged.
NIP98 URL/method/body/freshness/replay checks reject unauthorized requests at the public HTTP seam.
Missing/newer/inconsistent schema fails clearly instead of silently mutating startup state.

tickets.title: Upload and retrieve a verified original
acceptance: Invalid authorization is rejected before unbounded body receipt.
Hash/size failures, interrupted writes and duplicate retries cannot falsely register or double-charge an object.
Space is reserved atomically and only confirmed outcomes settle/refund it.
Stale cleanup cannot delete a newer generation; unregistered/staged objects are not anonymously exposed.

tickets.title: Project signed events through strfry
acceptance: Signature and identity validation precede persistence.
Duplicate events produce one durable intent; backend failure is reported with recoverable pending work.
Projection ordering and deletion/replaceable barriers are preserved without holding a database transaction across a subprocess.
Protected kind5 requests never enter the raw automatic-deletion import path.

tickets.title: Publish a complete immutable chapter
acceptance: Canonical CBOR, hash/version, descriptor and actual-image checks enforce the experimental profile.
Every unique original is verified, and conflicting repeated descriptors are rejected.
Deletion, eviction or revocation during preparation cannot cause stale completion.
A reader receives exact original bytes; static delivery can fall back safely while serving projections catch up.

tickets.title: Discover chapters with accepted filters
acceptance: Live offset/limit and inclusive signed-created_at bounds work together.
Exact non-language comparisons, RFC4647 basic ranges, unknown-under-NOT and explicit exists/missing agree across node and database evaluation.
Invalid, overbudget or oversized queries fail explicitly without partial-page success.
Explicit sort directions work; Q93/Q94 defaults remain provisional until answered.

tickets.title: Moderate protected publication removal
acceptance: Receipt alone does not auto-delete protected manga content.
Approval is local, deletion does not cascade automatically from series, and shared originals remain retained.
Completed withdrawal accounts for owned serving projections; interruption/retry is recoverable.
Replacement is a new upload/event, with no protocol revision/equivalence link.

tickets.title: Synchronize one approved peer chapter
acceptance: An unapproved peer or changed service key does not inherit access.
Signed event and manifest metadata are checked before downloading out-of-filter originals.
Only complete verified local originals become hosted on the receiver.
An independently approved fallback can repair a failed origin; arbitrary endpoints are not silently trusted.

tickets.title: Resume bounded large synchronization
acceptance: Discovery pages remain separate from bounded inventory snapshots.
Large/equal-timestamp inventories reconcile through validated partitions and explicit resource ceilings.
Lease loss, cancellation, retry and restart fence stale work and preserve idempotent admitted results.
Backoff, fairness and queue limits produce bounded behavior.

tickets.title: Publish for groups through member keys
acceptance: Publish and deletion-request signing use current role authorization, without exposing an arbitrary signing oracle.
Revocation persists after restart and is not reseeded from bootstrap configuration.
Signer references do not require plaintext private keys in PostgreSQL.
Key-only recovery preserves identity but does not recreate missing membership policy.

tickets.title: Maintain public libraries and social actions
acceptance: Replaceable snapshots and timestamp/ID ties behave deterministically.
Ordinary library/social NIP09 handling stays separate from protected-publication moderation.
Progress references exact publication IDs and public exposure is explicit.
No private-library or master-key subsystem is introduced.

tickets.title: Repair and reclaim stored originals
acceptance: Known corrupt/missing bytes cannot remain advertised as healthy through stale caches.
Shared references and active reservations/pins prevent unsafe reclamation.
Cleanup is fenced and idempotent; expiry alone does not refund uncertain writes.
Rotating bounded maintenance makes progress across the collection.

tickets.title: Import MangaDex-shaped exports
acceptance: Dry-run output identifies unsupported or ambiguous mappings before applying them.
Exact originals and chapter order are preserved without guessed associations.
Imported publications can be read and synchronized through the new node.
No real account access or catalogue scraping is required for the synthetic acceptance fixture.

tickets.title: Restore an interrupted instance
acceptance: Service identity, originals, tombstones, group revocations and public library state are preserved.
Old job ownership cannot resume against a newer restoration epoch without validation.
Accounting is reconciled and projection work resumes without duplicate publication.
Restore tests remain isolated and do not create an unintended live duplicate service.

tickets.title: Operate scalable serving roles
acceptance: Ordinary public image reads bypass PostgreSQL and Moka; guarded policies remain fail-closed.
Pool, worker, queue, body, decode and cache limits are explicit and observable.
Storage mutation ownership, generation fencing and API role separation do not rely on a global metadata mutex.
TLS/access-policy configuration fails safely; overload and backend outage have tested responses.

tickets.title: Verify PostgreSQL behavior end to end
acceptance: Legacy behavior contracts are rerun on the new stack rather than credited from SQLite results.
Cold/warm caches, competing writes, interrupted projections, corruption and restart are covered.
Experimental profile limits and remaining unsupported behavior are documented accurately.
The delivered archive rebuilds and its dependency graph contains no SQLx or SQLite in the selected server.

tickets.title: Finalize pending discovery defaults
acceptance: Accepted Q93D requires explicit order; Q94A provides optional exact totals with explicit budget errors.
Implementation, documentation and conformance tests match the chosen defaults.

tickets.title: Validate deployment capacity honestly
acceptance: Reusable workload drivers and acceptance metrics are ready and locally checked.
Cold/warm and concurrent read/write results identify hardware, dataset, network and cache assumptions.
Actual target-scale results require suitable infrastructure and permission; no synthetic result is labeled100TB validation.
Outstanding production/security/operational gates are reported rather than hidden.

tickets.title: Restore admitted publisher workflows
acceptance: An admitted non-admin publisher uploads a manifest and originals and publishes through signed HTTP; WS uses the same publication authority rules.
Logical publisher grants are independent of physical mutation ownership and bind the exact blob generation; another author cannot consume an ungranted staged original.
Permission epoch and grant validity are rechecked at the final commit; revocation, cancellation, duplicate uploads and shared hashes have negative/race tests.
Administrator, managed-group and approved-peer publication regressions still pass.

tickets.title: Complete staged blob lifecycle
acceptance: Bounded maintenance selects expired available never-published uploads; resumed work is idempotent and observable.
Authorized direct deletion of unreferenced uploads uses the existing durable receipt and accounting path.
Hosted publications, retained library objects, live grants, mutation generations and external-reader holds prevent premature deletion or refund.
Publisher and group grant expiry/release policies are explicit and tested; interrupted unlink/fsync/receipt and active publication races retain safety.

tickets.title: Isolate unsupported synchronization items
acceptance: Typed per-item outcomes distinguish unsupported contract, local-policy rejection, invalid content and retryable failures without matching error strings.
A mixed supported/unsupported inventory continues supported items and records durable bounded reasons for skipped items.
Batch status exposes skips/partial completion; unsupported items cannot exhaust retries and cancel unrelated partitions.
Lease, peer-revocation, cancellation, queue accounting and transient failure behavior retain explicit tests.

tickets.title: Complete Blossom browser interoperability
acceptance: A documented supported BUD subset defines standard upload, lookup and authorized deletion routes and signed-token scope.
Browser preflight, allowed origins and response-proof header exposure are configurable and tested.
Cross-origin handling does not grant publication, operator or deletion authority; negative origin and authentication tests pass.
A real client contract fixture exercises original upload/read/delete plus authenticated library requests.

tickets.title: Unify capability advertisements
acceptance: One typed registry drives namespaced NIP11 and HTTP application capabilities.
Endpoint, API/schema version, configured original format and query/body/admission limits match actual runtime behavior.
Unsupported versions and budget overruns produce explicit stable responses; advertised support has positive and negative contract tests.

tickets.title: Implement signed service discovery
acceptance: A service-key-signed replaceable endpoint list uses deterministic timestamp/ID selection and peer caching/exchange.
Expected keys are verified; first possession-verified identity is remembered when no expected key is supplied; a new key never inherits peer permissions.
URL safety, expiration/staleness and replay rules are explicitly resolved before implementing automatic endpoint use.
Domain move, transferred domain, old announcement replay and cold-peer discovery have tests.
tickets.remaining: Automatic configured-peer relocation and relay projection are not implemented.

tickets.title: Deliver multi-relay library clients
acceptance: A signer-agnostic client discovers selected write relays from NIP65 and sends identical signed chunked-library heads plus required objects.
First acceptance completes the initial save while other recipients retain separate bounded retries and visible outcomes.
A fresh device recovers the newest valid library from surviving write relays with deterministic replacement validation.
Offline recipients, conflicting heads, interrupted object delivery, revoked access and corrupted responses are tested without private-library scope.
tickets.remaining: Automatic NIP65 route-to-service binding remains open. Large30k/500k interrupted multi-batch recovery is verified.

tickets.title: Complete series metadata discovery
acceptance: Typed series/title/category contracts preserve accepted free-form categories and instance-local synonyms.
Public series and chapter discovery use parameterized bounded queries with accepted timestamp, ordering and three-valued filter semantics.
Cover and remaining metadata contracts are resolved explicitly; optional unknown fields are not silently reclassified as invalid.
Import round trips and positive/negative filter/search fixtures cover supported metadata.

tickets.title: Implement submission review workflows
acceptance: Unadmitted submissions have a bounded validated review path under local policy rather than automatic publishing authority.
Approval, rejection and expiry enforce publisher authority, original possession, storage budgets and durable audit outcomes.
Managed group backup and recovered-public-key registration have a usable offline runbook and verification fixture.
Action attribution requirements are resolved; portable membership export is not introduced as a mandatory protocol feature.
tickets.remaining: Admitted-account one-off submission review remains unimplemented; group action attribution is local operator-only.

tickets.title: Build MangaDex compatibility surface
acceptance: An explicit supported-client/endpoint matrix covers agreed browse/search/chapter/images, account/list/progress and publishing/group launch workflows.
Authentication and IDs are translated without reusing MangaDex credentials or inferring group control from display names.
Existing supplied-export migration retains exact originals and explicit public-history consent.
End-to-end compatibility fixtures establish advertised behavior; unsupported endpoints have honest explicit responses.

tickets.title: Harden restore serving defaults
acceptance: Restored configuration disables managed public serving until deliberate review/re-enable, alongside existing worker reset conventions.
An enabled-source serving backup/restore fixture covers path/port changes and preserves reader-hold safety.
Fault recovery distinctions are typed and observable; no timer alone clears holds or reopens serving.
Foreign host/namespace recovery limits remain documented unless a separately tested safe transition is implemented.

tickets.title: Verify complete backend contracts
acceptance: A requirement-to-wire-contract-to-implementation-to-evidence matrix covers every accepted in-scope feature and keeps unresolved choices explicit.
Large HTTP-module extraction and supervised-worker changes follow tested domain boundaries rather than speculative rewrites.
Functional regression, security-negative, crash/restart, TLS/reverse-proxy and cold-device recovery scenarios cover final code.
A source checkpoint rebuilds and is backed up; incomplete features and unproven capacity remain explicitly stated.

tickets.title: Complete reader account and library interfaces
acceptance: Account/profile, list and reading-state compatibility uses existing public signed identities and library graph.
Snapshot pinning, query budgets, read policy and signed write authority are preserved.
Actual HTTP tests exercise create/update/remove and access/replay/error cases.

tickets.title: Complete managed group public profiles
acceptance: Administrator-only kind0 profile updates retain protected group identity.
Revocation, compare-and-set, replay and atomic private audit are exercised.
Recovered group signing identity resumes with explicitly bootstrapped local administrator.

tickets.title: Make group publication retries stable
acceptance: Persisted caller timestamp and fixed publication payload retain Nostr event ID.
Retry after temporary grant expiry returns committed event without new storage or audit.
Current authority, review verdict and local removal remain enforced.
Checked API index includes all wrapper routes and current feature contract links.

tickets.title: Implement optional reader enrollment
acceptance: Disabled by default; only personal account permission granted.
Existing operator denials and mixed-version revocations cannot be undone.
Admission and signup-budget counters commit atomically with tested races.
Public policy discovery and signed metadata/library workflows verified.

tickets.title: Add approved peer WebSocket transport
acceptance: NIP42 and approved-peer allowlist protect a distinct read-only peer event interface.
Normal reader policy and publication/group signing authority remain unchanged.
Revocation, unauthenticated/unapproved keys and attempted writes are exercised.

tickets.title: Preserve retryable admission failures
acceptance: True missing/revoked authority stays403.
Account, group and peer permission database errors return503.
Metadata transaction failures are not invalid-client400 errors.
Fresh authorization retry succeeds after service-store recovery.
